newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Selective buying to underpin Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Selective buying to underpin Singapore shares.

text.p: Selective buying of blue chips and low-valued stocks was seen underpinning the Singapore stock market on Tuesday, dealers and analysts said.
"Some of the stocks are looking very attractive at current levels and it should be a good time to start accumulating," said Vasu Menon, research manager of Keppel Securities Ltd.
Among his recommendations were banking stocks like the foreign tranches of DBS, property counters like SingLand and electronic shares like FlexTech and Wong's Circuits.
Menon said SingLand was attractive as its price had fallen over 30 percent since February 20.
Menon added that the stock was unlikely to be dampened by rumours of further government measures in public housing.

On Monday, the Straits Times Industrials (STI) Index plunged to a 42-month low to end below its crucial 2,000 support for the first time since September 1993. It closed at 1,996.79, down 22.81 points or 1.13 percent.
Some analysts pegged the next support for the index at 1,950.
